problems.claim: Uniform real exponential bound plus pointwise holomorphy and c-continuity implies uniform bound in a complex neighborhood
problems.counterexample: E_z(c)=exp(-2xi|c|)exp(-c1^2 z^2) is entire and continuous; real weighted bound <=1; at z=i epsilon complex weighted bound and strip integral diverge.
problems.impact: Missing domination for Fubini/Morera and downstream BPZ/OPE continuation. Counterexample is to inference, not actual Toda integrand or final formula.
problems.repair: Establish a locally uniform complex-weight integrable majorant for the actual subtracted integrand and reflection terms away from poles.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Section2.4.7 p.34 explicitly makes the real-to-complex uniform-domination inference and uses it in Fubini/Morera. Lemma2.3 and the fixed-c regularization/real decay arguments pp.23-26 do not supply the missing locally uniform complex-weight c-integrable bound.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For xi>0 and c=(c1,c2), E_z(c)=exp(-2xi|c|)exp(-c1^2 z^2) is entire in z on a common domain and continuous in c. For every real z, |E_z(c)|exp(xi|c|)<=exp(-xi|c|)<=1, uniformly even over all real parameters.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Every complex neighborhood of0 contains z=i epsilon. Along c=(t,0), the weighted modulus is exp(epsilon^2 t^2-xi|t|), which is unbounded. The undamped c-integral also diverges on |c2|<=1 because the exponent is bounded below by epsilon^2 c1^2-2xi(|c1|+1). Thus all abstract premises of the printed inference hold but its conclusion fails.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This is a counterexample to the stated analytic inference, not to the actual Toda integrand. The actual expectation and reflection subtraction may have additional structure supporting a valid complex estimate. No claim is made that analytic continuation or the final formula is false.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The missing domination underlies Theorem2.2 and the BPZ continuation pp.36-38, OPE continuation pp.55,59,65 and shift argument p.70. A demonstrated gap at this core analytic step is Major without requiring whole-paper failure.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Prove a locally uniform complex-weight integrable majorant for the actual subtracted integrand, including reflection terms and uniformity away from poles. Fixed-c holomorphy and real exponential decay alone do not provide it.

problems.location: p.35 (3.4)–(3.7); p.38 Proposition 3.2/(3.12); pp.40–41 connection calculation
problems.claim: Printed D_i weights yield single-valued hypergeometric solution
problems.counterexample: Exact gamma/sine cancellation requires lambda_i D_i=lambda_0. A=(epsilon,1/4,1/3),B=(1/2,3/4),0<epsilon<1/8 satisfies all nonresonance assumptions; D1~C/epsilon versus required reciprocal ->different. Explicit epsilon=1/100 60-digit check retained.
problems.impact: False intermediate BPZ formula/monodromy coefficients; affects coefficient identification and shift ratios. Final FL formula not disproved.
problems.repair: Use reciprocal coefficients for the stated unscaled H_i; audit every shift equation and Upsilon comparison. Also correct infinity prefactor (-z)^A_i to (-z)^(-A_i).

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: The unscaled H0,H1,H2 are defined on p.35, and Theorem3.1/(3.6)-(3.7) and Proposition3.2/(3.12) print D_i rather than reciprocals. On p.40 tilde-lambda_i=lambda_i D_i, while p.41 concludes lambda0=tilde-lambda1=tilde-lambda2. The infinity prefactor in(3.13) also has the opposite sign from the indicial roots.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: A=(epsilon,1/4,1/3), B=(1/2,3/4), 0<epsilon<1/8 makes all six numbers0,B1,B2,A1,A2,A3 distinct modulo integers and all differences real, exactly as Proposition3.2 requires. All relevant gamma factors are finite and nonzero. B1,B2<1 makes the corrected normalized solution continuous at0 with value1.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: For an infinity basis G_i~(-z)^(-A_i), the H0 connection coefficient is K0i=Gamma(B1)Gamma(B2) product_(j!=i)Gamma(Aj-Ai)/[product_(j!=i)Gamma(Aj)Gamma(B1-Ai)Gamma(B2-Ai)]. The other rows follow by A->1-Bk+A and B->(2-Bk,1-Bk+B_other); their common modulus-one phases cancel in the Hermitian form. Gamma reflection reduces vanishing cross terms to lambda0 sin(x)sin(b1-b2)-lambda1 D1 sin(b1-x)sin(b2)+lambda2 D2 sin(b2-x)sin(b1)=0. Nonresonance gives lambda0=lambda1 D1=lambda2 D2, hence coefficients D_i^(-1). This diagonal form is invariant at0 and infinity, hence also at1, and gives an actual solution under the proposition's assumptions. D1~C/epsilon with C>0, whereas the required coefficient tends to0. At epsilon1/100, the current80-digit calculation gives printed cross terms about -63798,39994,-89922 and reciprocal residuals below3e-82. The analytic sine identity is exactly zero. Separately, the dominant infinity equation has exponents -A_i, confirming the prefactor sign error.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The high-precision test is corroborative rather than a certified interval proof. The exact connection/sine argument and nonresonant epsilon family establish the intermediate error. A specific physical Toda correlation or the final Fateev-Litvinov expression is not thereby disproved. The gamma reflection identity itself is correctly printed.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The explicit BPZ/monodromy coefficients feed OPE coefficient matching p.55, the shift relations p.70 and comparison with the Upsilon expression p.69. False intermediate coefficients in this core derivation justify Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use reciprocal coefficients for these stated unscaled H_i and correct the infinity prefactor. Recompute all affected A/B conventions, OPE matches, shift ratios and Upsilon comparisons; replacing one coefficient is not a certified repair of the whole derivation.

problems.location: p.50 Section 4.2.1 unnumbered integral immediately before (4.12)
problems.claim: Bare diagonal integral is absolutely integrable for gamma>1
problems.counterexample: Near x=y=1/2, radial factor int_0^eta r^(1-2gamma^2)dr diverges. gamma=6/5, q=43/15, alpha0=(2/gamma-delta,q-delta), alpha=(-gamma,0), alpha1=(0,q-delta), alphaInf=(q-delta,2/gamma-delta) in fundamental-weight coordinates satisfy A4 and extra hypotheses for arbitrarily small generic 0<delta<1/100.
problems.impact: Invalid O(z^2) remainder domination in core OPE proof. Does not prove original damped expectation diverges.
problems.repair: Retain damping or prove suitable diagonal fusion bound with z-uniform and c-integrable estimates.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: The unnumbered integral on p.50 immediately before(4.12) is the bare double integral with |x-y|^(-2gamma^2), explicitly called absolutely integrable to obtain O(z^2). Lemma4.2's local assumptions and nearby restrictions pp.42-44,48-50 were read with the A_N conventions p.14.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Root normalization is Cartan[[2,-1],[-1,2]], fundamental-weight Gram[[2/3,1/3],[1/3,2/3]], q=gamma+2/gamma and Q=q(omega1+omega2). For gamma6/5,q43/15, the report's weights alpha0=(5/3-delta,q-delta), alpha=(-6/5,0), alpha1=(0,q-delta), alphaInf=(q-delta,5/3-delta) have strict positive root deficits and s.omega1=-47/45-7delta/3>-gamma, s.omega2=14/45-8delta/3>0 for0<delta<1/100. They also satisfy kappa<q, gamma<alpha0.e1<2/gamma and the stated proximity conditions as delta approaches0. To keep other insertions fixed, set eta=1/1000 in alpha1=(0,q-eta), alphaInf=(q-eta,5/3-eta), leaving delta only in alpha0. Then s.omega1=-2353/2250-delta>-gamma and s.omega2=557/1800-delta>0. Arbitrarily small irrational delta meets any positive proximity threshold and avoids the remaining rational-affine pole equations. Exact checks over all6^4 Weyl tuples and both fundamental-weight pairings find no identically imposed s(w) pole in either family.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: On a small patch near x=y=1/2, the other absolute factors in the printed integrand are bounded above and below by positive constants. The relative coordinate therefore contributes integral_0^eta r^(1-2gamma^2)dr, divergent for gamma>=1; at gamma1 the divergence is logarithmic and at6/5 its exponent is -47/25. This obstruction is independent of the insertion exponent and all sufficiently-close thresholds.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The actual expectation before discarding exponential damping can remain finite. Divergence of the bare bound does not establish divergence of the original stochastic quantity, falsity of Lemma4.2's conclusion, or falsity of the final formula. The parameter verification concerns this local OPE regime; it does not assert every reflected tuple belongs to the final theorem's domain.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The false absolute-integrability claim is used for an O(z^2) remainder in the core OPE proof before(4.12), hence Lemma4.2 and Theorem4.1. Major for the demonstrated core derivation error.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Retain the damping in the estimate or supply a genuine diagonal fusion bound that is uniform in z and integrable in the zero mode c. The bare singular kernel cannot serve as that majorant for this gamma range.

problems.location: p.18 (2.33),(2.34); counterevidence p.18 following sentence and p.27
problems.claim: Maximum of thresholds suffices for positive GMC moments
problems.counterexample: gamma=1,alpha=Q-(1/2)omega1-(7/4)omega2,p1=1,p2=0 satisfy printed bounds; mean integral 2pi int_0^1 r^(-3/2)dr diverges.
problems.impact: False auxiliary moment range; actual explicit p.27 first-moment use is within valid regime, so additional core harm not established.
problems.repair: Enforce bulk and each insertion threshold jointly; verify joint moment statement against precise external lemma.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: The maximum/vee is printed in both(2.33) and(2.34), p.18. The normalized GMC convention p.11 and the actual first-moment use p.27 were checked.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Take gamma1,q3, alpha=Q-(1/2)omega1-(7/4)omega2, giving alpha.e1=5/2 and alpha.e2=5/4 with both root deficits positive. p1=1,p2=0 satisfy the printed maximum thresholds, since max(2,1/2)=max(2,7/4)=2. This lies in the subcritical GMC range.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The normalized GMC has Lebesgue first moment on the unit disc. Tonelli therefore gives expectation of the first insertion integral as integral_|x|<1 |x|^(-5/2)dx=2pi integral_0^1 r^(-3/2)dr=infinity. Other separated insertions are bounded on the same local patch, so the local obstruction also affects(2.33). The printed sufficient moment condition is false.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The following sentence correctly requires insertion deficit>gamma for the first moment, and the explicit p.27 use satisfies that stronger condition. No additional core failure is established. The external joint-moment lemma was not completely reread in this acceptance.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: An erroneous auxiliary admissible range with demonstrated counterexample, but a correct nearby first-moment statement and valid traced application; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Require the bulk and every insertion restriction jointly. Verify the exact joint positive-moment theorem against its precise external hypotheses before claiming a complete replacement range.

problems.location: p.55 Lemma 4.3 and (4.13); related p.49 Taylor subtraction
problems.claim: Printed plus first-order subtraction yields ordinary convergent integral for 0<a-b<1
problems.counterexample: a=3/2,b=1 satisfies all assumptions; numerator ~-2cos(theta), sector absolute integral grows as int^infty r^(-1/2)dr.
problems.impact: Literal integral undefined; localized counterterm sign error, with explicit integrability repair. Circular principal value is not stated.
problems.repair: Change first-order sign inside r_ab to minus, propagate corresponding Taylor sign and verify coefficient calculation.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Lemma4.3 p.55 assumes a<2,b>-2,a-b>0 excluding1,2 and defines r_(a,b) with a plus first-order term in the regime0<a-b<1. Related Taylor subtractions on p.49 were checked.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: a3/2,b1 gives a-b1/2 and satisfies every printed condition. For x=r exp(i theta), |x-1|=r-cos(theta)+O(1/r), while the printed r_(a,b)=r+cos(theta).
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The numerator is -2cos(theta)+O(1/r). On a fixed sector with cos(theta)>1/2 its absolute area integral is bounded below by a positive multiple of integral^infinity r^(-1/2)dr; the opposite sector has the opposite sign. Thus the ordinary Lebesgue integral is undefined, not merely non-absolutely convergent. No circular principal-value convention is stated. Replacing the internal first-order plus by minus cancels the linear term and leaves O(r^(b-2)); the corrected radial tail is r^(-(a-b)-1), integrable for a-b>0. In the active counterterm regime0<a-b<1, the origin terms have radial powers1-a,1-(a-b),-(a-b), all integrable under a<2; near x1, b>-2 suffices.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: A circularly truncated principal value can behave differently, but that is not the claimed ordinary integral. The explicit sign correction restores the relevant integrability and is separate from the diagonal-bound failure in P3.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: A local Taylor-counterterm sign error with a controlled integrability repair, rather than an established independent failure of the final coefficient formula; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Change the first-order sign inside r_(a,b), propagate the corresponding Taylor sign on p.49, and recheck the gamma evaluation and matching calculation. Their full corrected coefficient derivation is not claimed completed.

independent_acceptance_scope: Focused independent verification of every reported P1-P5 against the exact acquired arXiv:2208.12085v3, including conventions, domains, quantifiers, nonresonance, proof dependencies and boundary cases. This is not a fresh complete 73-page review, a complete recursive external-reference audit, or certification of journal-version equivalence.
